proposals.title: Append-only evidence-event log with inclusion, consistency, and equivocation witnesses
proposals.boundary: Earlier phases covered ancestry, manifests, hash parity, atomic receipts, requirement-evidence traces, citation anchors, redirects, and source aliases; none tested append-only inclusion plus cross-size consistency and explicit equivocation while separating log membership from claim truth.

proposals.title: EFT operator-basis quotient under integration-by-parts and equation-of-motion redundancy
proposals.boundary: The chain tested variational traces, field-redefinition orbits, Bianchi exchange, hyperbolicity, kinetic-Hessian rank, constraint closure, and degree-of-freedom counting; it did not quotient an explicit operator list by integration-by-parts and declared equation-of-motion redundancy.

proposals.title: Cutoff hierarchy and EFT truncation-error promotion lock
proposals.boundary: Earlier proposals covered solver tolerances, dimensional typing, prior sensitivity, posterior prediction, calibration covariance, measurement error, and stability; none enforced a declared EFT cutoff and order-by-order truncation remainder with an explicit empirical-promotion lock.

proposals.title: Pre-decode instrument-drift and measurement-invariance gate for THOS
proposals.boundary: Prior THOS work covered allocation, power, attrition, carryover, interference, multiplicity, exposure escrow, scorer reliability, safety stopping, protocol deviations, and estimands; none froze instrument structure and measurement-invariance criteria before arm decoding.

proposals.title: Challenge-domain freshness and verifier-audience replay boundary for Freed ID
proposals.boundary: Earlier Freed ID proposals covered lifecycle, rotation races, holder binding, purpose-bound methods, selective disclosure, status privacy, resolver egress, schema downgrade, and cryptosuite agility; none bound one-use challenge freshness simultaneously to domain, verifier audience, purpose, and time window.

proposals.title: Burden-of-proof, unknown-state, and evidentiary-silence non-substitution gate
proposals.boundary: Prior CBR proposals addressed rights floors, standing, remedy, consent withdrawal, empty chairs, dissent, recusal, delegated sunset, data sovereignty, wording scope, jurisdiction, and forum competence; none isolated evidentiary-state semantics and prohibited technical burden-of-proof or adverse-inference substitution.

proposals.title: Unicode confusable skeleton, normalization-version, and cross-artifact identifier tribunal
proposals.boundary: Earlier security work covered Unicode parsing validity, path aliases, reserved names, streams, reparse points, parser depth, adversarial encodings, and oracle poisoning; none pinned a Unicode confusable-skeleton profile for cross-artifact identifier identity while separating identifiers from natural-language text.

proposals.title: Floating-point edge-case and comparison-policy replay envelope
proposals.boundary: Prior reproduction work covered tolerances, intervals, environment perturbations, time and locale, seed lineage, PRNG versions, manifests, hashes, and dual oracles; none froze signed-zero, NaN, infinity, ULP, cancellation, summation-order, and comparison-policy semantics as one replay contract.

proposals.title: Path-dependence, hysteresis, and state-function non-substitution barrier
proposals.boundary: Earlier thermo-psyche proposals covered entropy domains, measurement scales, aggregation levels, causal direction, promotion burdens, open systems, stock-flow, and state-rate typing; none tested path dependence, trajectory reversal, hysteresis, and state-function non-substitution together.

proposals.title: Reversibility-class ledger and irreversible-action authority embargo
proposals.boundary: Prior Stage 20 work covered expiry, evidence order, cut sets, non-compensation, contradiction lattices, evidence classes, escrow, asymmetric loss, abstention, and reopening; none made action reversibility, rollback evidence, blast radius, and irreversible external-state authority a single embargo contract.
